model_annotation: The image presents three distinct pie charts illustrating the distribution of quantifiers and logical operations across different reasoning categories in the R2I-Bench benchmark for reasoning-driven text-to-image generation. The first chart, labeled “Categorical,” is divided into four segments: Universal Quantifiers (29.07%, light blue), Negation (27.91%, orange), Limiter (27.91%, light pink), and Existential Quantifiers (15.12%, light green), with the largest segment being Universal Quantifiers and the smallest being Existential Quantifiers. The second chart, “Approximate Number Generation,” contains three segments: Approximate Quantities (45.03%, beige), Comparative Relationships (36.26%, light blue), and Absolute Absence (18.71%, light purple), with Approximate Quantities forming the largest portion. The third chart, “Disjunctive & Conjunctive,” is split nearly evenly between two segments: Conjunctive (50.49%, light pink) and Disjunctive (49.51%, light blue), with Conjunctive holding a slight majority. Each chart uses distinct pastel colors for its segments and includes percentage labels within each slice, providing a clear visual breakdown of the proportional representation of each category.
